questions.question: Prime cost is:
options: Direct materials plus direct labour — the costs that touch the product directly

questions.question: The wages of a supervisor watching six production lines are classified as:
options: Indirect labour, included in factory overheads

questions.question: Rent of the sales office is:
options: An administration cost — the word FACTORY in factory overheads matters

questions.question: The three stocks of a manufacturer are:
options: Raw materials, work-in-progress and finished goods

questions.question: Opening raw materials R80 000, purchases R640 000, carriage R20 000, closing raw materials R120 000. Direct material cost is:
options: R620 000 — materials available less what remains unused on the shelf

questions.question: Prime cost of R1 000 000 plus factory overheads of R440 000 gives:
options: Cost of production of finished goods

questions.question: Opening work-in-progress was R60 000 and closing work-in-progress R100 000. The adjustment to total manufacturing cost of R1 440 000 gives cost of production of finished goods of:
options: R1 400 000 — add the opening, subtract the closing

questions.question: Cost of production R1 400 000 for 70 000 finished units gives a unit cost of:

subtopics.title: From Factory Floor to Income Statement

questions.question: Opening finished goods R90 000 plus cost of production R1 400 000 less closing finished goods R140 000 gives cost of sales of:
Sales of R2 160 000 against cost of sales of R1 350 000 confirms a mark-up on cost of:
options: 60 percent — gross profit of R810 000 over cost of sales

questions.question: Depreciation on delivery vehicles belongs in:
options: Selling and distribution cost — classified by what the spending served

questions.question: When one building houses the factory and the office, rent is split by:

subtopics.title: Break-Even and the Ethics of Making Things

questions.question: Selling price R32, variable cost R21 per unit, fixed costs R660 000. The break-even point is:
options: 60 000 units — fixed costs divided by the contribution of R11

questions.question: Producing and selling 67 500 units against a break-even of 60 000 means:
options: The business runs at a loss
A cushion of 7 500 units, each contributing R11 of pure profit
Fixed costs are not fully covered

questions.question: If raw materials become more expensive while price stays fixed, the break-even point:
options: Climbs — the contribution per unit narrows, so more units are needed to cover fixed costs

questions.question: Competitors agreeing with each other on selling prices is:
options: Price fixing — illegal collusion against the consumer

questions.question: In Auntie Grace's kitchen, the flour, sugar, oil and syrup are:
options: Direct materials — they become the product

questions.question: The gas bottle and stand rent are overheads because:
options: Nobody can say which koeksister used which rand of them — real costs, spread over everything

questions.question: At ten o'clock, the braided dough waiting for the oil is:
The notebook Auntie Grace writes orders in belongs to:
options: The business-running costs — office, not kitchen

questions.question: Auntie Grace bought R7 000 of ingredients but R1 000 remains in the cupboard. The month's materials cost is:
options: R6 000 — the cupboard's contents cost nothing to this month's koeksisters

questions.question: Kitchen total R14 000, opening dough tray R400, closing dough tray R600. Finished production cost is:
options: R13 800 — add the opening tray, leave out the closing one

questions.question: R13 800 of finished production across 2 300 koeksisters gives a unit cost of:
options: R6 — and selling at R10 leaves R4 of gross margin each

questions.question: The grandson's question really taught that:
options: Unit costs only matter to factories
Money spent this month and production finished this month are different things — the cupboard and the dough tray hold the difference

subtopics.title: How Many Must She Sell Before She Smiles?

questions.question: Rent of R4 000 a month and a contribution of R5 per koeksister give a break-even of:
options: 800 koeksisters — number 801 is the first that feeds the family

questions.question: The proof that 800 is break-even is:
options: 800 times R5 equals R4 000 of profit
R8 000 in from sales, R4 000 of ingredients and R4 000 of rent out — exactly zero

questions.question: If syrup prices push variable cost to R6 per koeksister, break-even:
options: Jumps to 1 000 — the contribution narrows to R4

questions.question: Opening a second stand with R4 000 more fixed rent illustrates that:
options: Fixed costs fall as businesses grow
Growth raises the pile to cover before the first extra unit sells — the break-even doubles
